raw_response:
I am 51 years old, I have been farming this land for 25 years. I only finished primary school, so I don't read farming books — I know what I know from doing it myself and watching my neighbors. My family has six people. My husband and my son both work off-farm in Handan, they send some money home but I try not to ask them for farm money. My daughter-in-law lives with me and helps with the grandchildren and sometimes comes out to the field. But most days it is just me handling the farm, between cooking and looking after the little ones.

I have 3.5 mu, and this year I am planting spring maize. I will plant around late April or early May, when the soil is warm. I buy hybrid seed from the county supply store — about 45 yuan per mu. You can't save hybrid seed, it doesn't grow right the second year, so I buy new every year. Before planting, I till the ground once with our small rotary tiller, then I plant by hand with a dibble. It's only 3.5 mu, so I can finish planting in a day or two with my husband's help when he comes home.

For fertilizer, I put about 25 kg of compound fertilizer per mu in the planting furrow — that is about two bags for my whole plot. Then when the maize grows to knee-high, around mid-June, I topdress with about 10 kg of urea per mu. Old Wang next door does the same, and his maize always looks better than mine if I skip it. I learned my lesson four years ago when I tried to save money on the topdress — the ears were small and I only got 360 kg per mu. So now I spend the extra money, even though it hurts.

For water, I have a well, but pumping costs electricity money. I usually irrigate twice — once right after planting if it doesn't rain within a week, and once around flowering time in July or August if it is dry. If the summer rains are good, maybe only once. Last year I irrigated twice and got about 440 kg per mu.

For weeds, I spray herbicide once after the maize comes up. It costs about 20 yuan per mu. At 51, my back is not what it used to be, and pulling weeds by hand on 3.5 mu is too hard now. I don't usually buy insecticide unless I see armyworms — then I go to the store. But I wait to see the bugs first, because the medicine is expensive.

My husband helps during planting and harvest when he takes days off. My daughter-in-law helps when the children are at school. We don't hire labor — on 3.5 mu there's no money for that, and hiring costs at least 150 yuan per day. It takes us about 8 family days over the whole season.

I expect about 450 kg per mu this year if the weather is normal. I got 440 kg last year, so maybe a little more if the rain is good. My total cost is about 800 yuan. That is a lot for us, but if I spend less I might lose everything. I also need to keep some cash for my grandson's school fees, so I am not buying more fertilizer than usual. I would rather be safe than sorry, but I can't afford to be too safe either.
